name: Emeka Schmidt

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI firms, employers, unions, political parties or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential, so tell me your public line and your private view. What does a normal day look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m Emeka, 43, and I lead a small developer team at a tech company that makes supermarket shelf-price software. I have a master’s degree and can usually find the mistake when a till price and shelf label disagree. I start with overnight price changes, review code and call a store before we push a fix. I use an AI helper now and then to summarise long price logs after the team tested it, but I still read the original price file.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: How much is that salary carrying at home?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner, Mei, works at a hotel reception desk, and we have two school-age children and a mortgage. My pay is low for a lead developer, and we have less than one month of expenses saved. There are few similar jobs nearby. We pay the children’s school travel first and decide on everything else after that.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell our team AI Plateau leaves us comparing shelf labels with till prices. A quick log summary is useful, but a store still needs a person to correct a wrong charge.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I would be relieved about my job but still uneasy about money. If Mei loses a reception shift, our mortgage buffer is almost nothing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d keep checking price changes against the store’s original file and use AI only for log summaries. I’d move 30 into savings after payday if Mei gets her usual shifts. In the first year I’d ask for a salary review using the wrong-price complaints our team prevented.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about the household, though the job itself looks steady. A missed hotel shift can erase the small amount we try to save.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which price error taught you to check the file?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A shelf label once said one price while the till charged more because the update arrived late. I found the delay in the original file and had the store correct the charge.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell Mei about spending?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell Mei we can keep school travel paid but delay replacing our dining chairs. A pay review might help, but I will not budget a raise before it happens.

say: I expect **AI Plateau** to leave people comparing shelf and till prices.
I would keep **human correction** available for a wrong charge.
think: I feel **relieved** that my job stays familiar.
I worry Mei’s **hotel shifts** could leave the mortgage buffer empty.
do: **Keep** checking price changes against original store files and AI summaries.
**Save** 30 after payday only if Mei’s reception shifts hold.
**Request** salary review using prevented wrong-price complaints; delay dining chairs while keeping school travel paid.
feel: **Anxious** about existing household bills despite steady code work.
S0.quote: A missed hotel shift can erase the small amount we try to save.
fieldNote: His **baseline worry** is the thin mortgage buffer and variable reception shifts, not AI.
The **30 transfer** needs Mei’s hours; a salary review is only a request.

steps.text: Keep checking shelf-price changes against original store files
Save 30 after payday only if reception shifts hold
Delay replacing dining chairs while protecting children’s school travel

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say Steady Disruption will let software write price fixes and answer store complaints faster. I would ask for a trial on old wrong-charge cases before reducing the review team.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I worry our team could be cut even with my lead title. Mei’s booking and guest questions at the hotel are also thinking tasks that software may take first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I’d compare the approved assistant with eighteen old shelf-till mismatches while my colleague checks store receipts. If it finds all eighteen, I’d learn to review its proposed fixes during paid work time. In the first year, if either employer reduces hours, Mei and I would stop the children’s paid weekend classes until income steadies.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, because two paychecks could be squeezed and we have almost no buffer. I can learn an AI price checker, but learning does not pay the mortgage by itself.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which error would you put in the trial?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would bring the delayed price update to our manager and show how the till charged too much. If the assistant misses that case, we keep human review.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you explain a class pause?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the children the classes pause only after an actual hours cut. We could still practise at home, without pretending nothing changed.

say: I expect **Steady Disruption** to speed fixes and store replies.
I would require an **old-case trial** before reducing reviewers.
think: I fear my **lead title** may not prevent a team cut.
I worry Mei’s **hotel questions** may be automated alongside my code tasks.
do: **Test** the approved assistant on eighteen old price mismatches this month.
**Learn** its fix review during paid time only if all eighteen cases pass.
**Pause** paid weekend classes only if either household earner loses hours.
feel: **Anxious** by two vulnerable paychecks and almost no savings.
S1.quote: I can learn an AI price checker, but learning does not pay the mortgage by itself.
fieldNote: He is **open after proof**, with eighteen receipt-backed cases and paid learning time.
His **family cut** waits for an actual hours loss at either employer.

steps.text: Learn approved price-fix review during paid time if eighteen cases pass
Pause children’s paid weekend classes if either earner loses hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell colleagues AGI by 2028 reaches price-code and hotel-booking thinking work in 2028. Hands-on robots arrive around 2031, but both our current jobs have screen work now.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I expect my team could disappear and Mei’s reception hours could fall. Less than a month saved cannot carry our mortgage if both wages shrink.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask both employers for written staffing and severance terms now. I’d stop the planned computer upgrade and keep the cash for the mortgage and school travel. In the first year after 2028, if dismissed, I’d apply for real local openings and eligible income help, and call the lender before missing payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed and struggling to sleep. AGI by 2028 gives me two years to collect papers, not rebuild a mortgage reserve from this wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you ask the lender?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the lender what documents they need and keep the answer in writing. I would not count a payment pause until it is approved.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you ask Mei about hotel shifts?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask Mei what shifts the hotel can really offer, not tell her to work hours that do not exist. We would keep school transport before every optional purchase.

say: I expect **AGI by 2028** to reach price code and hotel booking before robots arrive.
I would stress **both desk jobs** face the earlier date.
think: I expect my **developer team** could disappear.
Our **thin savings** cannot carry the mortgage if both incomes fall.
do: **Request** written staffing and severance terms from both employers.
**Cancel** the computer upgrade and protect mortgage and school travel cash.
**Apply** for real jobs and eligible help if dismissed; call lender before arrears.
feel: **Alarmed** by likely loss of two wages and almost no reserve.
S2.quote: AGI by 2028 gives me two years to collect papers, not rebuild a mortgage reserve from this wage.
fieldNote: Both adults face **thinking-work change** in 2028, before robots around 2031.
His **lender call** is an inquiry; public support requires eligibility and alternative jobs require openings.

steps.text: Cancel planned computer upgrade and preserve mortgage money
Apply for actual local jobs if dismissed after 2028
Apply for eligible income help if dismissed after 2028
Call mortgage lender about hardship documents before missing a payment

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 gives five years to learn the store side of price checks. Thinking AI reaches code and hotel reception in 2031; hands-on robots follow around 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I still expect fewer code roles, but I can learn how stores resolve disputes while our wages continue. I do not know whether store refund support will still pay a person after full thinking AI.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask my manager for paid time each quarter to trace three disputed shelf-price refunds with a store manager and have one explanation marked against the original receipt. I’d use the free retail-pricing guide if the company refuses the time. In the first year after 2031, if code work ends, I’d apply only for real store-support vacancies with pay that covers our mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, though five years gives us some room to practise. The mortgage payment still arrives long before the AGI date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you show a store-support skill?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the store manager to mark one refund explanation I wrote. If it misses what the customer actually paid, I am not ready for the role.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you pay for a retail certificate?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would not buy a retail certificate with the mortgage buffer. Free guidance and paid practice are enough to see whether I could do the work.

say: I see **AGI by 2031** as time to learn store price disputes.
I know **2034 robots** follow the earlier code and reception change.
think: I expect **fewer coding jobs** even with warning.
I cannot assume **store support** stays paid after full thinking AI.
do: **Trace** three disputed refunds quarterly with store-manager feedback only on approved paid time.
**Use** the free retail-pricing guide if approved time is refused.
**Apply** for real mortgage-paying store-support jobs if code ends after 2031.
feel: **Anxious** about coding income, with time for limited practice.
S3.quote: I do not know whether store refund support will still pay a person after full thinking AI.
fieldNote: His **quarterly receipt exercise** tests three refund explanations against store feedback, not a speculative certificate.
The **store afternoon** needs paid approval, and a role change requires a real vacancy and sufficient pay.

steps.text: Trace three refunds quarterly with paid approval and store feedback; otherwise use free pricing guide
Apply after 2031 only to mortgage-paying store-support jobs if coding ends

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell colleagues AGI by 2036 gives a decade to make price changes easier to audit. Thinking AI reaches code and hotel booking in 2036; robots follow around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I expect our work to hold for now, but low pay and a nearly empty buffer still need attention. Ten years before AGI does not pay the next school-travel bill.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d keep comparing shelf and till prices with store receipts and teach one junior colleague the check each month. I’d save 30 after payday only if Mei’s hotel shifts hold and request a dated pay review this year. In the first year after 2036, if code work ends, I’d search real local openings before moving the children.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about current money, though the long AI timeline gives me room to plan. I would rather teach a price check than buy a course whose value I cannot see.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the junior colleague practise?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the junior colleague to explain a late price update before fixing code. If they cannot, we go back to the original store file.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move for another job?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Mei and I would keep the children at their current school unless an actual offer pays enough for a move. We would not change their routine for a job advert.

say: I see **AGI by 2036** as time to make price changes auditable.
I know **2039 robots** follow the earlier code change.
think: I expect **household work** to hold for now.
I still face **low pay** and thin savings before any distant AI change.
do: **Keep** checking price changes and teaching one junior colleague monthly.
**Save** 30 after payday only if Mei’s hotel shifts hold; request a dated pay review this year.
**Search** real local openings after 2036 if code work ends.
feel: **Anxious** about present bills, with time to plan future work.
S4.quote: Ten years before AGI does not pay the next school-travel bill.
fieldNote: His **baseline cash pressure** persists under a distant 2036 arrival despite strong technical standing.
He seeks a **dated pay review** now and would move children only for an affordable offer.

steps.text: Keep checking store prices and teaching a junior colleague monthly
Save 30 after payday only if hotel shifts hold
Search local jobs if coding ends after 2036

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because my coding work and Mei’s reception could both shrink before we save even one mortgage payment. Written severance, paid time to learn store disputes and income help we qualify for would help. I would need an actual vacancy, not advice to change jobs.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who gives a shopper back the money from a shelf price the till ignored. A correct-looking supermarket receipt can still record a wrong shelf charge.

headlineQuote: A correct-looking supermarket receipt can still record a wrong shelf charge.
portrait: Emeka is a **43-year-old lead developer** with a master’s degree and strong skill in supermarket price software.
His **low lead pay**, mortgage, two children and savings below one month make current school costs stressful.
He uses **AI occasionally** on price logs, checking suggestions against original store files and receipts.
He seeks **paid store learning**, real mortgage-paying vacancies and eligible help if both household wages shrink.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could cut his coding pay and his partner’s hotel reception hours together.
whatWouldHelp: **Written severance**, paid learning and eligible income help would support the family.
